correctness.rationale: The stationary reflecting Neumann heat kernel has endpoint covariance h(u)=2Σ_{n≥1}exp(-n²π²u) for u≥0, and the even kernel has L1 norm 4Σ1/(n²π²)=2/3. Young convolution yields Var(H_t)≤(2/3)∫κ², asymptotically sharp for constant κ. Since κ≤K, Var(H_t)/A(t)²≤(2K)/(3A(t)); a subsequence with A(t_j)≈j² and monotonicity yields H_t/A(t)→1 a.s. if A∞=∞, hence zero eternal survival. A∞<∞ implies E H∞=A∞<∞ and E exp(-H∞)>0. Nonoverlapping C∞ pulses at integer centers with area one, width 2^(-4j), and amplitudes increasing produce summable endpoint-hit probabilities O(sqrt(width)), so only finitely many pulses contribute a.s.; yet E H∞=Σ1=∞, and E exp(-H∞)>0. Independent Neumann spectral partial sums and exact calculations verify covariance constants and finite survival arithmetic. No finite experiment was used for infinite proofs.
